source.title: A Study of Fitness Landscapes for Neuroevolution
source.authors: N. Rodrigues; Sara Silva; L. Vanneschi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; figure plots are garbled in places, but the prose and Table III are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses selective walks and fitness-landscape measures to test whether those measures predict neuroevolution's training and test performance; it does not test the claim versions' specified interventions or comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on natural-label image datasets, but does not test arbitrary-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, CNN-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer or batch comparisons, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its loss-trajectory and autocorrelation comparisons bear on test generalization but do not measure the named effects in V1–V8. Those results are recorded under fits_no_version. Figure-only autocorrelation boxplots are not transcribed as numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates selective-walk autocorrelation and entropic ruggedness as indicators of CNN neuroevolution performance. Neither measure tests V7's magnitude-scaled weight perturbations or ranking of generalization gaps. Natural-label loss trajectories alone do not test V1–V6 or V8. Wilson et al. is cited for SGD, without an adaptive-versus-SGD comparison or explicit reliance on its generalization finding.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that autocorrelation and entropic ruggedness are reasonable indicators of neuroevolution problem hardness on both training and test sets. They frame this as a proof of concept and call for larger samples and more problems.
record.recipe_differences: Grammar-based CNN neuroevolution with SGD-trained individuals, selective walks, and landscape statistics; it is not a test of the claim's standard gradient-training interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and mutation type change optimization difficulty and the landscape statistics; autocorrelation behavior also varies with step size, with longer steps often more informative for hard problems.

fits_no_version.finding: Best-individual training and test loss trajectories vary with dataset and mutation operator. The authors explicitly describe similar training/test behavior on MNIST and FMNIST; CIFAR-10 learning mutations show greater diversity on the test set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dataset and mutation operator affect training and held-out loss trajectories in grammar-based CNN neuroevolution.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning mutations have the lowest Rf on every dataset, ranging from 0.28 to 0.41. Topology mutations have the largest maximum, 0.50, but parameter mutations have higher Rf than topology mutations on MNIST and FMNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mutation operators alter selective-walk entropic ruggedness; topology mutations are not uniformly the most rugged by Rf.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report qualitative correspondence between selective-walk autocorrelation and neuroevolution difficulty on training and test sets, with longer lags often more informative for hard configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective-walk autocorrelation can indicate optimization and held-out performance of the tested CNN neuroevolution configurations.

record.problems: The authors characterize this as a proof of concept; only four datasets, 10 walks and 10 evolutionary runs per configuration, short walks of length 30, and 20 generations are used. The text says larger and more significant samples are needed. Loss trajectories and autocorrelation boxplots are figure-only, without recoverable numerical values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure-only autocorrelation results were not given separate rows because the claim versions do not cover fitness-landscape autocorrelation as a predictor; their stated qualitative role is summarized in fits_no_version and page excerpts.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning; optimizer repairs and switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes; batch size is fixed at 64.
Controlled dropout addition/removal, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay. Dropout is available in the grammar but its held-out effect is not isolated.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similar training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Identification and removal of highly memorized examples compared with equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All row-version links remain none. The original tests label and T2 tranche are inappropriate because the study's predictive landscape measures address a different question. No verdict follows from the mere inclusion of dropout, evolving layer sizes, or using SGD.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold.
CNN versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum under tuning regimes.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout addition/removal and its effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with other generalization measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random examples.

rows.subject: neuroevolution of CNNs using learning mutation on MNIST
rows.stage_stated: 20 generations; each network trained for 8 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Evolutionary training with learning mutations; best-individual loss trajectories reported for training and test sets.
rows.measure: Training and test loss trajectory of best individual; exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: 10 independent runs; no numeric uncertainty stated
rows.note: Authors state the problem is easy on both sets and that training and test results are very similar for practically all runs.
rows.check: Training/test loss trajectories do not measure any named version; observed is not a claim-relative state here.
